newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caribbean top-ups maintain Venezuela oil exports.
newsitem.headline: Caribbean top-ups maintain Venezuela oil exports.

text.p: Venezuela's oil exports from Lake Maracaibo are being maintained by using Caribbean oil storage terminals as top-up points after shipping was restricted in the Lake Maracaibo channel, oil traders said on Tuesday.

Since a 3.5 foot draught reduction was imposed on April 18, Venezuela's state oil company PDVSA has been using storage in Curacao and Bonaire to top up partly-filled cargoes after they leave the Lake, they said.

The channel draught was cut from 39.5 to 36 foot at high tide after ship pilots protested at three groundings this year, one of which produced a 25,000 barrel oilspill. The channel is used for 70 percent of the country's crude exports.

The largest tankers to use the channel normally load up to 650,000 barrels of crude using the full draught of 39.5 feet, but the restriction means they now take only about 500,000 barrels, shippers say.
PDVSA is sending the top-ups of heavy crude to Bonaire and light crude to Curacao using its own fleet of tankers.
PDVSA traders say they may start loading larger, million barrel ships from these terminals to save money on freight, which has risen since the draught restriction was imposed.
Shipping agents expect the port captain to increase the draught from 36 to 37 feet at high tide when a survey of the channel floor has been completed in the next week or so.
The Bonaire BOPEC terminal, with 10 million barrels capacity, is a PDVSA subsidiary and the Curacao terminal, with 11.5 million barrels capacity, is leased by PDVSA.
